Figure 2. ScreenDrag Automated Data Collection Pipeline. ScreenDrag automated data generation pipeline for continuous trajectory-
based GUI interaction data. The pipeline includes three stages: (i) Element Parsing: The software application UI is parsed with UI
                           SDK in order to retrieve the UI element metadata, i.e., bounding box, etc. (ii) Task Proposal: Given the UI
Automation of Windows[(0,1327,542),(1,1556,542),(1,1510,542),(1,1463,542),(1,1417,542),(1,1373
element metadata, an LLM ,542)]will be prompted to generate a drag instruction, i.e., reduce the image width by 0.4 from its right, and the
                         [(1327,542), (1556,542), (1510,542), (1463,542), (1417,542), (1373,542)]
expected metadata change. Afterwards, the corresponding drag code with dense trajectory will be generated. (iii) Trajectory Synthesis:
The drag code will be executed in the software environment. A rule-based verifier will check the parsed metadata from UI states before
and after the drag to ensure that the metadata change satisfies the expectation.

                                                                                       Clicks and drags exhibit different temporal and spatial dy-

and efficient trajectory generation—we adopt a flow-                                                                                                                                                                    ries that closely follow the instructed paths.

correct cursor orientation or jitter. To explicitly regularize                                                                                                                                                          we limit each baseline to three interaction steps.

How do chunk size and execution steps impact model                                In Fig.1, we demonstrate how ShowUI-π produces precise
performance? As shown in Tab. 6, increasing chunk                                 trajectory generation aligned with task intent across differ-
size, i.e., length of steps in each prediction, from 10 to                        ent domains. In PowerPoint, the model accurately performs
20 generally boosts the performance, indicating predicting                        the required 45-degree clockwise rotation, producing a tra-
more action steps is helpful for learning to capture the ac-                      jectory consistent with the instructed geometric transform.
tion distribution. Interestingly, when the execution steps are                    In Handwriting, it generates a smooth, continuous stroke
large, i.e., executing more steps from prediction before the                      that clearly forms the intended “S” shaped curve in “Star-
next re-observation, increasing chunk size can help alleviate                     lit grin.” For Captcha, the model exhibits fine-grained con-
the degradation. When the execution steps are 5, increasing                       trol, stopping at the exact rotation angle needed to solve the
chunk size from 10 to 20 can improve its accuracy by 12.9%                        puzzle rather than overshooting. These results collectively
and reduce trajectory error by 36.4 px. Moreover, fewer ex-                       show that ShowUI-π can follow continuous, high-degree-
ecution steps generally produce the highest accuracy and                          of-freedom motions with instruction-following.
least error, showing that frequent re-observation enhances                        6. Conclusion
